comparison: Perfect agreement on mitochondrial morphology characterization (C1-C6). Both evaluations find the structural measurements well-supported. OpenEval emphasizes statistical rigor and sample sizes, while peer reviewers praise the 'careful analysis' and note EM as 'gold standard.'

Complete agreement on spine mitochondria findings (C7-C13). Both evaluations support the characterization of spine mitochondria as distinct from dendritic mitochondria. OpenEval highlights statistical testing and sample adequacy, while peer reviewers accept findings without challenge.

Agreement on mitochondrial proximity methodology (C14-C20). Both evaluations support the approach. OpenEval validates the choice of measurement radii, while peer reviewers accept findings but suggest considering absolute distances as potential improvement.

Strong agreement on lack of correlation between mitochondrial volume and structural synaptic strength (C21-C26, C62). Both evaluations endorse this key negative finding. OpenEval notes it challenges initial hypothesis, while peer reviewers call it 'surprising' and 'compelling' evidence that will 'inspire rethinking.'

Agreement on spine neck length correlations (C27-C29). Both evaluations support findings. OpenEval notes reliance on prior literature (Turner et al., 2022) for mechanistic explanation, while peer reviewers accept without challenge.

Strong agreement on functional diversity correlation (C30-C35, C60). Both evaluations strongly endorse this central finding. OpenEval emphasizes bootstrapping methodology and replication across cells, while peer reviewers call evidence 'compelling' and 'informative' for understanding mitochondrial function.

Divergent evaluations of weak correlations (C36-C40). OpenEval rates UNCERTAIN due to weak effect sizes (|r|<0.2), marginal significance (p~0.03), and speculative mechanistic interpretation. Peer reviewers rate SUPPORTED without raising concerns about correlation strength or multiple testing.

Strong agreement on heterogeneous spine cluster findings (C41-C46, C61, C63). Both evaluations strongly endorse this major finding. OpenEval highlights strong correlation (r=0.563) and effective control analyses, while peer reviewers call it 'intriguing' and 'compelling' evidence for specific functional roles.

Agreement on calcium transient correlations (C47-C51). Both evaluations support findings. OpenEval notes moderate negative correlation at 5 µm and inferential mechanistic interpretation, while peer reviewers accept calcium buffering explanation without challenge.

Agreement on spine mitochondria structural and functional associations (C52-C58). Both evaluations support findings. OpenEval addresses C52-C55 (structural) while peer R10 covers C52-C58 (structural and functional), both finding evidence well-supported for distinct roles of spine versus dendritic mitochondria.

Partial overlap on spine mitochondria functional properties (C56-C58). OpenEval R11 focuses on functional selectivity differences, while peer R10 includes these claims alongside structural findings. Both support the interpretation of distinct functional roles.

Agreement on computational methodology (C82, C120) but different emphases. OpenEval notes lack of validation metrics and contradictory 'unsupervised' terminology despite requiring training data. Peer reviewers praise the methodology as 'state of the art' and highlight dataset strengths without raising technical concerns.

Partial overlap on main conclusions. OpenEval R13 synthesizes conclusions (C60-C63) noting correlative nature. Peer R6 addresses C60 alongside primary data (C30-C35), strongly endorsing functional diversity findings as 'informative.'

Partial overlap on conclusions about lack of structural correlation (C62). OpenEval R13 synthesizes this as main conclusion, while peer R4 addresses it alongside primary negative findings (C21-C26), calling it 'surprising' and 'compelling.'

Partial overlap on conclusions about functional diversity support (C61, C63). OpenEval R13 notes conclusions are well-supported but correlative. Peer R8 strongly endorses these conclusions as 'compelling' evidence for specific functional needs.

Peer reviewers raised concerns about functional measurement limitations (C97-C100) that OpenEval did not address. Reviewer 1 noted GCaMP6s only measures some Ca signals and orientation tuning may not optimally evaluate synaptic strengths, rating these claims UNCERTAIN.
